traceability.evidence:
Key implementation: - ESLint rule src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts implements validation that @story annotations reference existing story files with correct .story.md extension. It: - Parses @story lines from all comments (handleComment, validateStoryPath) - Resolves paths using context.cwd (falling back to process.cwd) plus configurable storyDirectories and flags allowAbsolutePaths/requireStoryExtension - Applies security checks (performSecurityValidations) to block disallowed absolute paths and traversal, then extension checks via hasValidExtension, and finally existence + boundary checks via normalizeStoryPath and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence - Reports clear diagnostics through messageIds fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, and fileAccessError, each including the offending path (and error) in the data
Supporting utilities (src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts, src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts): - buildStoryCandidates() builds candidate absolute paths from cwd and storyDirectories, respecting explicit ./ and ../ semantics (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS) - enforceProjectBoundary() and analyzeCandidateBoundaries()/handleProjectBoundaryForExistence() ensure resolved paths stay within project root and treat out-of-project candidates as invalidPath even if the filesystem says they exist (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION) - Caching of fs checks via fileExistStatusCache with __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests() (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION) - Robust, non-throwing filesystem handling in checkSingleCandidate(), getStoryExistence(), and storyExists(), classifying statuses as exists/missing/fs-error and surfacing a representative error where appropriate (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) - Security helpers isAbsolutePath, containsPathTraversal, hasValidExtension, isUnsafeStoryPath enforce path and extension constraints (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION)
Tests (tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts): - File header explicitly ties tests to docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md and requirement IDs (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY) - RuleTester suite "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)": - Valid cases: correct .story.md references and ./ relative paths - Invalid cases: missing files → fileMissing, wrong extensions → invalidExtension, traversal and disallowed absolute paths → invalidPath - Additional RuleTester suites cover: - Configurable storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, and requireStoryExtension (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS) - Rejection of out-of-project absolute paths and misconfigured external storyDirectories (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY) - Jest-only tests "Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries" and "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling" verify: - storyDirectories-based resolution - Absolute-path handling within project - Boundary behavior when normalize or config would escape cwd - storyExists behavior when fs throws (EACCES/EIO) – never throws, returns false - Rule’s reporting of fileAccessError with error details when filesystem operations fail (permissions, I/O errors) (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, user-facing diagnostics)
Documentation (docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md): - Describes the rule, explicitly referencing story 006.0 and REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE / REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION / REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION - Details project-boundary behavior, differentiation between fileMissing/invalidExtension/invalidPath/fileAccessError, and configuration options storyDirectories/allowAbsolutePaths/requireStoryExtension, matching the story’s implementation notes and examples (Documentation acceptance criterion)
Test run: - npm test -- --runInBand --verbose executed successfully (exit code 0) - Jest output shows all suites, including: - "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" - "Valid Story Reference Rule Configuration and Boundaries (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" - "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" - All tests passed (38 suites, 290 tests total)
Together, the rule implementation, utilities, tests, and docs directly address all the enumerated requirements and acceptance criteria for story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION are satisfied. The valid-story-reference rule validates that @story paths exist and use the .story.md extension, integrates with prior annotation format validation, enforces security and project-boundary constraints, caches filesystem checks for performance, and provides clear, specific error messages including fileAccessError for filesystem issues. Tests explicitly mapped to this story and its REQ IDs comprehensively cover file existence, path resolution, error handling, security, project boundaries, and configurable paths, and all pass. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md describes the behavior and configuration in line with the story. Therefore the story is fully implemented.
